prompt: Why does a carboxylic acid show a VERY broad O–H band from 2500–3300 cm⁻¹, while an alcohol's O–H is only moderately broad (3200–3550)?

options.label: COOH exists as H-bonded cyclic dimers; the two strong H-bonds span a wide range of O–H distances, broadening the band.
The COOH O–H sits next to a heavier C=O, which lowers its reduced mass and spreads the frequency range.
COOH protons exchange rapidly between neighbors, averaging shifts across a broad window.
Alcohols form ordered H-bonded hexamers, giving sharp bands; carboxylic acids form random long chains with varied H-bond strengths.

explanation: COOH forms cyclic H-bonded DIMERS held together by two strong, short H-bonds. The large anharmonicity means O–H samples many bond lengths → extremely wide absorption (2500–3300). Alcohols just H-bond in disordered chains with narrower spread. Rapid exchange and reduced mass don't explain the width.
